overview: Sri Kaleshwara Mukteswara Swamy Temple, popularly known as Kaleshwaram Temple, is one of the most ancient and revered Shiva temples in Telangana. Situated at Kaleshwaram in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, it stands at the Triveni Sangamam — the confluence of the Godavari, Pranahita and the mystical Saraswati rivers. The temple is uniquely dedicated to two Shiva Lingas, Lord Mukteswara and Lord Kaleshwara, installed together on a single pedestal, a feature believed to symbolise liberation (Moksha) and protection from the cycle of birth and death. Devotees from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh visit throughout the year for health, prosperity, spiritual growth and salvation.
summary: Sri Kaleshwara Mukteswara Swamy Temple at Kaleshwaram, Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, Telangana, is an ancient Shiva temple famed for its unique twin Shiva Lingas (Mukteswara and Kaleshwara) on a single pedestal and its location at the Triveni Sangamam of the Godavari, Pranahita and mystical Saraswati rivers. Dating back over a thousand years and flourishing under the Kakatiya dynasty, it is associated with the legend that Lord Yama installed the Kaleshwara Linga. The Mukteswara Linga has two nostril-like holes through which abhishekam water is believed to flow into the Sangamam. It is a major centre for Moksha-seeking worship, ancestral rituals (Pitru Karmas), and the grand Maha Shivaratri festival.

history.content: The temple's history dates back more than a thousand years and is closely associated with ancient Shaivite traditions. Historical records suggest it flourished during the rule of the Kakatiya dynasty, whose kings constructed and renovated several Shiva temples across the Telugu region. Over the centuries the temple has undergone multiple renovations while preserving its original spiritual significance.
history.foundation_year: Over 1,000 years (flourished under the Kakatiya dynasty)
legends: The temple is named for its twin deities — Mukteswara (giver of liberation) and Kaleshwara (associated with time and death).
Two Shiva Lingas on a single pedestal are found only at Kaleshwaram.

history.content: According to temple legends, Lord Yama, the God of Death, installed the Shiva Linga of Lord Kaleshwara at this sacred site after worshipping Lord Mukteswara to seek liberation from the burden of taking away human lives. Because Lord Yama himself performed penance here, devotees believe worshipping at Kaleshwaram frees them from the fear of death and grants spiritual liberation.
legends: Lord Yama installed the Kaleshwara Shiva Linga after worshipping Lord Mukteswara to be freed from the burden of taking human lives.
Worship here is believed to free devotees from the fear of death.

sthala_puranam: Lord Yama, the God of Death, worshipped Lord Mukteswara here to seek liberation from the burden of taking human lives, and installed the Shiva Linga of Lord Kaleshwara. The two lingas — Mukteswara (liberation) and Kaleshwara (time and death) — share a single pedestal, unique to this temple. The Mukteswara Linga bears two nostril-like holes through which abhishekam water is believed to flow down into the Triveni Sangamam beneath the temple, a phenomenon regarded as divine. Per Tripadvisor HARAGOPAL 4/5 review, 'Muktheswara (Whose Two nostril hols can NEVER be completey filled with water (Any amount of water you pour)'.
religious_significance: Kaleshwaram is one of the holiest Shiva temples, where devotees seek blessings for long life, freedom from sins, peace and ultimate liberation (Moksha). The worship of Mukteswara and Kaleshwara together symbolises divine grace and liberation from worldly attachments. The Triveni Sangamam (Godavari, Pranahita and the mythical Saraswati) makes a holy dip here highly meritorious, and the site is a major centre for ancestral rituals (Pitru Karmas).
spiritual_significance: The temple's most distinctive feature is the twin Shiva Lingas on a single pedestal, found nowhere else. The Mukteswara Linga has two nostril-like holes through which abhishekam water is believed to flow into the Triveni Sangamam beneath the temple. Devotees believe a holy dip at the Sangamam before darshan washes away sins, and that performing Pitru Karmas (ancestral rituals) at the confluence brings peace to departed souls and blessings to families. Worship is believed to free devotees from the fear of death and grant Moksha.

architecture: The temple showcases a blend of ancient South Indian temple architecture and the artistic excellence of the Kakatiya period. Located on the banks of the Triveni Sangamam, it features beautifully carved stone pillars, traditional mandapams, and a towering Rajagopuram. The sanctum houses the unique twin Shiva Lingas — Lord Mukteswara and Lord Kaleshwara — on a single pedestal, the only such arrangement in India. The complex includes shrines to Goddess Parvati, Lord Ganesha, Lord Subrahmanya, Nandi and other deities, and a separate Saraswathi Ammavari Temple.

darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: General darshan is free of cost for all devotees.
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Special darshan and Arjitha Sevas are available to reduce waiting time.
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Tickets for Rudrabhishekam, Abhishekam, Archana, Laksha Bilwarchana and other sevas can be purchased at the temple counters. During Maha Shivaratri and Karthika Masam, special crowd-management arrangements and additional darshan facilities are provided.

dress_code: Devotees are encouraged to wear traditional and modest attire. Men generally wear dhoti, kurta or other traditional Indian clothing; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez or other decent traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless tops and revealing outfits are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering, silence should be maintained in the sanctum, and photography may be restricted in certain areas.

accommodation.availability: The temple provides temple-managed guest houses and dharmashalas with clean, affordable rooms, plus Telangana Tourism (Haritha) accommodation. Private budget, family and premium hotels are available near the temple and in nearby towns such as Mahadevpur, Manthani and Ramagundam (premium options in Ramagundam, Mancherial and Karimnagar).
accommodation.booking_process: Rooms can be enquired about at the temple office or booked via online travel portals; advance booking is strongly recommended for Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Pushkaralu.
accommodation.first_come_basis: Limited walk-in accommodation may be available at temple counters on a first-come basis, but advance booking is strongly recommended during festivals and weekends.
accommodation.price_range: Temple guest rooms generally ₹200–₹800 per day (deluxe/family rooms higher). Private hotels and lodges usually ₹800–₹2,500 per night.
nearby_options: Budget, family and premium hotels in Mahadevpur, Manthani and Ramagundam
Premium hotels in Ramagundam, Mancherial and Karimnagar

best_time_to_visit: October to March (October–February excellent) for pleasant weather. Best days: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday; best time 6:00–8:00 AM, evening option 4:00–5:30 PM. Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Shravana Masam are the most auspicious but most crowded times.

travel.road: Approximately 270 km from Hyderabad via Karimnagar and Manthani (5–6 hours). TGSRTC operates regular buses from Hyderabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Mancherial, Ramagundam, Peddapalli, Jagtial and Bhupalpally; APSRTC services connect from Andhra Pradesh. Special buses run during Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Saraswati Pushkaralu.
travel.rail: Nearest stations (distances conflict between source sections): Peddapalli Junction (~85 km / ~110 km), Mancherial Railway Station (~65 km / ~95 km), and Ramagundam Railway Station (~100 km). All are well connected to Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Chennai, Nagpur, Delhi and Visakhapatnam.
travel.air: Nearest airports: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~290–300 km), and Nagpur Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport (~310 km). Taxis, rental vehicles and intercity buses are available from both.

travel_tips: Begin the journey early, especially on weekends and major festivals.
Carry drinking water, comfortable footwear (for walking outside) and basic medicines, particularly in summer.
Take a holy dip at the Triveni Sangamam before entering the temple if possible.
Arrange accommodation in advance for Maha Shivaratri and Karthika Masam.
Early morning (6:00–8:00 AM) offers peaceful darshan; prefer Tuesday–Thursday for lower crowds.
Take enough cash beforehand — no ATMs available in Kaleshwaram (per Tripadvisor Sujeet N C 5/5).
Make sure enough fuel in your vehicle — no fuel stations within 30 km radius (per Tripadvisor review).
Stock up on home-made food — limited and basic food options in Kaleshwaram (per Tripadvisor reviews).
Carry your own pooja items (coconut, flowers, agarbatties) — shops at the ghat may charge high rates (per Tripadvisor review).
Boating on the river is available and recommended (per Tripadvisor reviews).
Mobile cameras should not be used inside to preserve sanctity (per Tripadvisor reviews).

top_reviews: Tripadvisor (BAPrakashReddy, 5/5, 'A HOLY -- KALESHWARAM TEMPLE'): 'Visit the temple early mornings for a quicker darshan, prasad is served fresh, there are authorized locker facilities and shoe keepers outside. Abstain from from using mobile cameras to preserve sanctity inside. An important religious town in Karimnagar district of Telangana province adjoining Maharashtra and Adilabad province has Lord Shiva as its main deity. Before entering the temple the devotees takes a holy bath at the river and do the pooja for river. There are 2 siva lingas are placed in the single base in which one is shiva and the another one is yama(god of death). Because of these two lingas the temple is termed as kaleshwara muktheswar temple. The temple is located in the place where 3 rivers are flowing together. In these three we can able to see 2 rivers; one is godavari from telangana and the other is pranahita from Maharashtra and the remaining river is saraswathi which is believed that it flow under those both rivers. Most of the water comes from pranahita during non rainy season also. Even in summer also the water flow is around 15 to 20 fts in the middle of the river. Boating also available for both the ends.'

Tripadvisor (Sujeet N C, 5/5, 'Kaleshwaram Temple'): 'An important religious town in Karimnagar district of Telangana province adjoining Maharashtra and Adilabad province has Lord Shiva as its main deity. Rivers Godavari, Pranahita and another tributary join here which is considered auspicious and unique as much as the presence of 2 Shiva Lingas. Lord Yama is also revered here along with Lord Shiva. Temple: Visit early mornings for a quicker darshan, prasad is served fresh, there are authorized locker facilities and shoe keepers outside. Desist from using mobile cameras to preserve sanctity inside. Place: Serene, windy banks on the river front, well preserved environs and forests. Food: Not the best you may expect, small places serving hot puri curry in mornings, South Indian thali at lunch and dinner. So stock up on home made food beforehand. People: Friendly, all religions and faiths live together. Precautions: Take enough cash beforehand as no ATMs there, make sure enough fuel in your vehicle as no fuel stations in a radius of 30 km. Constructive criticism: Authorities need to curtail VIP visits causing inconvenience to common people in the temple, establish at least 1 ATM and 1 fuel station, construct good flooring around the temple environs for smooth walking, establish parks instead of permitting new constructions in the town area. This will help towards making this a neat place for visiting public and preserve the historic importance for the deities.'

Tripadvisor (HARAGOPAL, 4/5, 'UNIQUE TEMPLE'): 'One of the Unique and ancient temples of Lord Shiva where Two Lingams, one installed by YAMA (God of death) called KAALESWARA and the other Muktheswara (Whose Two nostril hols can NEVER be completey filled with water (Any amount of water you pour). Located on the banks of river GODAVARI, one must visit this temple.'

Bus stand is at a walkable distance from temple. Sign boards are proper for rooms booking place.'

Before entering the temple the devotees takes a holy bath at the river and do the pooja for river. Boating also available for both the ends. Because of these two lingas the temple is termed as kaleshwara muktheswar temple. The connectivity and facilities are to be improved.'

Google Maps (Local Guide, 5/5): 'Unique temple with two Shiva Lingas on a single pedestal — one of them has two nostril-like openings through which abhishekam water flows into the Triveni Sangamam. The location is divine — at the confluence of Godavari, Pranahita and the mystical Saraswati. Boat rides on the river are a great experience. introduction.en: Sri Kaleshwara Mukteswara Swamy Temple at Kaleshwaram in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, Telangana, is an ancient Shiva temple famous for its unique twin Shiva Lingas — Mukteswara and Kaleshwara — installed on a single pedestal, and for its location at the Triveni Sangamam of the Godavari, Pranahita and the mythical Saraswati rivers. Dating back over a thousand years and flourishing under the Kakatiya dynasty, it draws devotees seeking liberation, health and prosperity.

history.en: The temple dates back more than a thousand years and flourished under the Kakatiya dynasty, who built and renovated many Shiva temples in the region. According to legend, Lord Yama, the God of Death, worshipped Lord Mukteswara here to seek liberation from the burden of taking human lives, and installed the Shiva Linga of Lord Kaleshwara. The two lingas share a single pedestal, a feature unique to this temple.

travel_guide.en: Kaleshwaram is about 270 kilometres from Hyderabad via Karimnagar and Manthani, a five to six hour journey, with regular TGSRTC buses. The nearest railway stations are Peddapalli, Mancherial and Ramagundam, roughly 85 to 110 kilometres away. The nearest airports are Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, about 290 to 300 kilometres away, and Nagpur, about 310 kilometres. The temple is open from 4:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:30 PM; October to March is the best season. Take cash and fuel beforehand — no ATM and no fuel station in 30 km radius of Kaleshwaram.

faq.question: Where is Sri Kaleshwara Mukteswara Swamy Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located in Kaleshwaram village, Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, Telangana, near the Triveni Sangamam.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Mukteswara and Lord Kaleshwara, two Shiva Lingas installed on a single pedestal.

faq.question: What is special about Kaleshwaram Temple?
faq.answer: It is famous for its unique twin Shiva Lingas on a single pedestal and its location at the confluence of the Godavari, Pranahita and the mystical Saraswati rivers (Triveni Sangamam).

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: The temple is generally open from 4:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:30 PM, though timings may vary during festivals.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No. General darshan is free, while special sevas and rituals require separate tickets.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Maha Shivaratri is the grandest festival, attracting lakhs of devotees from different states.

faq.question: Are accommodation facilities available?
faq.answer: Yes. Temple guest houses/dharmashalas, the Telangana Tourism (Haritha) hotel and several private hotels and lodges are available near the temple.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Kaleshwaram Temple?
faq.answer: The best time is from October to March, especially during Maha Shivaratri and Karthika Masam.
